editorial:
Imagine a world where a crude, loud butcher suddenly becomes a millionaire because of the chaos of World War I. That is exactly where you land with Rupp, a man who has all the money in the world but none of the class. He is obsessed with his son, Fred, who loves cars, but Rupp also sets his sights on Helen, a poor former noblewoman. Helen is desperate to save her sick mother, so she agrees to marry this uncouth man just for the cash. It is a messy setup full of greed and secret grudges, creating a vibe that feels like a high-stakes soap opera from a century ago.

You will probably be surprised by how well the acting holds up, especially since it is a silent film. The tension between Rupp and his enemies keeps the story moving quickly. While some parts feel a bit slow due to the old style of filming, the drama is top-notch. If you enjoy stories about social climbing and betrayal, you should definitely check this one out.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when the secrets come out. You see Rupp realize that his own son, Fred, is actually in love with Helen and wants her to be with Platen instead. The greed of the shyster Graf also catches up with him. In the end, the money cannot buy Rupp the love or respect he craves. The marriage plans crumble, leaving Rupp alone with his wealth while the younger couple finds a way to be together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school dramas and stories about rich people behaving badly.
